paper.title: The internal spatial organization of firms: Evidence from Denmark
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement and no Statistics Denmark project reference. …

registers.name_in_paper: Integrated Database for Labor Market Research (IDA)
registers.role: sample frame, linkage, outcomes (establishment counts, employment shares, establishment size); contains all matches between employees and their workplaces with unique firm, establishment and worker identifiers
worker occupation, aggregated into six categories (managers, business services workers, engineers and scientists, clerical workers, production workers, other workers)
firm records: value of production, total employment, firm sector, and the firm-reported location used to identify the HQ (municipality level only)
firm accounting records: value of production, employment, sector and firm-reported location
controls / worker characteristics: highest completed education level

registers.name_in_paper: National Transport Model (LTM), Technical University of Denmark
registers.years: 2017 version of the model, applied to 1981-2016 establishment locations
registers.role: treatment-relevant geography: the location of all establishments at the traffic-zone level (907 traffic zones), and the distance and travel time between all pairs of traffic zones as well as average travel times within zones

linkages: Establishments, firms and workers are linked by the unique identifiers in IDA, which allow following every worker through every establishment and firm in Denmark
IDA is merged with a novel dataset containing the location of all establishments at the traffic-zone level (built on the National Transport Model, LTM)
IDA is merged with the Labor Classification Module (AKM) for worker occupations, and with the Population and Education Statistics registers for age and education
IDA is merged with firm records from the General Firm Statistics (FIRM) and the Accounting Statistics (FIRE), whose firm-reported location identifies the HQ municipality
An establishment is defined as the unique triplet of establishment identifier, location and firm identifier

An establishment is categorized as the HQ if its location equals the location the firm reports and it has at least five employees; this defines a HQ for 96% of the firms in the sample, and for the remaining 4% the establishment with the largest number of (i) managers, (ii) high wage earners, (iii) workers with master's or doctorate degrees and (iv) workers with technical or bachelor's degrees is chosen

sample.universe: The universe of employers and employees registered in Denmark between 1981 and 2016 (90,165,404 worker-years, 6,657,020 establishments and 5,237,107 firms in the economy; 60,346,107 / 5,646,343 / 4,827,549 in the private sector), restricted to the private sector and to firms in manufacturing, transportation, business services, and finance, insurance and real estate (FIRE)
sample.unit_of_observation: firm-year (also establishment-year and worker-year, depending on the exercise)
selection_rules: Keep private-sector firms only (the public sector accounts for around 30-35% of all full-time employees)

Keep firms in manufacturing, transportation, business services, and finance, insurance and real estate (FIRE); exclude farming, fishing, raw material extraction, energy/water supply, disposal, construction, wholesale, retail, hotels, restaurants, and culture and leisure
Drop establishments with no reported location and establishments located in Fanø, Læsø or Christiansø
Drop establishments that only appear one year
Drop firms that had fewer than 4 employees for more than 66% of their lives in the database
Drop establishments with fewer than 3 workers (1 or 2 employees)
Drop firms with outliers in changes in the number of establishments across years
Drop firms with 99 or more establishments
Keep workers between 15 and 80 years old, using each employee's main job as defined by Statistics Denmark on the basis of the worker's main source of income
sample.period: 1981-2016 (1991-2016 for everything using occupations, since DISCO is only available from 1991)
sample.n_observations: 688,958 firm-year observations, 871,673 establishment-year observations and 25,397,415 worker-year observations (Table A5; Table A1 reports 25,391,415 worker-years in the sample column)
sample.n_individuals: 70,736 firms and 67,032 establishments in the two-way fixed effects regressions (Table A2); on average per year 19,138 firms, 24,213 establishments and 705,484 workers (around 42% of the private labor force)

construction_notes: Distances and travel times are computed between traffic zones (907 zones, average area 47.3 km2, against 424.3 km2 for the average municipality; 9.25 traffic zones per municipality on average) using the National Transport Model; travel times are a function of road size, quality and congestion, and within-zone average travel times are included

The average and median establishments of ME firms are located 127 km (93 min) and 70 km (57 min) from their HQ; the maximum distance (travel time) between an establishment and its HQ is 788 km (810 min)

The average-distance measures include the distance of the firm's HQ to itself (a zero), which lowers the baseline distances and could inflate percentage changes; Fig. 6 Panel B and Fig. A9 recompute them excluding the HQ
Weighted averages weight each establishment by its relative size (share of the firm's workers) within the firm

4-digit DISCO codes are aggregated into six categories (Table A4): managers (1000-1999), production workers (60-83, 92-93), business services workers (2400-2419, 242, 2440-2449, 3400-3439, 344, 346-347), clerks (243, 40-52, 90-91), engineers and scientists (200, 21, 220-222, 231, 311-312, 32), and other workers; the classification changed from DISCO88 to DISCO08 between 2009 and 2010 and a crosswalk (available on request) is used

Commuting areas are those defined by Nielsen (2005); establishment location is observed at the traffic-zone level while the firm-reported HQ location is observed only at the municipality level for confidentiality reasons

Establishments outside Denmark and arm's-length transactions inside the country are not observed, so the results are interpreted as a lower bound of the actual decentralization and specialization patterns

Sample representativeness (Fig. 3, Table A1): the share of ME firms in the sample is 5-6.5 percentage points larger than in the whole economy, and the shares of employment and production generated by ME firms are also larger, but their evolution is almost parallel; sample workers have slightly higher education, experience and tenure, with production and business services workers and engineers and scientists slightly overrepresented and managers and clerical workers underrepresented

claims.statement: The number of multi-establishment firms in Denmark rose from 4,500 in 1981 to almost 11,000 in 2016.

definition.value: Calendar year; the reported estimate is the change in the yearly cross-sectional sample mean of the outcome between 1981 and 2016

outcome.label: Total number of multi-establishment (ME) firms in Denmark

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research): unique firm, establishment and worker identifiers

definition.value: Count of firms registered in Denmark with more than one establishment, by year

units.value: number of ME firms in 2016 (from 4,500 in 1981)

magnitude.interpretation: it went from 4,500 (3.3% of the total number of firms) to almost 11,000 firms (7.4%)

estimand.target_population: Private-sector Danish firms in manufacturing, transportation, business services and FIRE that satisfy the paper's selection criteria

population.description: Firms (and their establishments) registered in Denmark in the private sector in manufacturing, transportation, business services and finance, insurance and real estate (FIRE), after the Appendix B.2 selection steps
population.selection: Private-sector firms in manufacturing, transportation, business services and FIRE; establishments with no reported location or on three small islands dropped; establishments with 1 or 2 employees or appearing only one year dropped; firms with fewer than 4 employees for more than 66% of their existence dropped; firms with more than 99 establishments or large jumps in the number of establishments dropped (Appendix B.2, Table A5)

identification.source_of_variation: Year-to-year variation in cross-sectional sample means over 1981-2016; within-firm change and changes in the composition of firms are not separated

key_assumptions.assumption: The yearly cross-sectional averages are read as describing the economy as a whole; the paper states that their evolution also reflects changes in the composition of firms in the economy and not only change within firms
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper re-estimates the same quantity with firm fixed effects and compares the two

key_assumptions.assumption: The averages are computed on the selected sample (private-sector firms in manufacturing, transportation, business services and FIRE surviving the Appendix B.2 filters), not on the universe of Danish firms
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table A5 reports the observations left after each selection step

implies_edges.from: sample selection (Appendix B.2 filters: four sectors, activity and outlier restrictions)
implies_edges.to: Total number of multi-establishment (ME) firms in Denmark

key_assumptions.assumption: Establishments that Danish firms may have outside Denmark, and arm's-length transactions inside the country, are not observed, so the measured decentralization and specialization are a lower bound on the actual patterns

Statistics Denmark's definitions of firms and establishments did not change over 1981-2016 in a way that affects the results (the paper notes the firm fixed effects also help control for such changes)

threats_discussed: Changes in the composition of firms in the economy (entry and exit) contaminate raw-data averages: most entering firms are single-establishment and new firms are more compact
Establishments of Danish firms abroad and arm's-length transactions inside Denmark are unobserved, so the patterns are a lower bound
The average-distance measures include the distance of the HQ to itself (zeros), which lowers baseline distances and could inflate percentage changes
Possible changes over time in the way Statistics Denmark defines establishments
Including the HQ in the distance measures versus excluding it changes which firms contribute (excluding the HQ drops firms that go from one to multiple establishments)
robustness_checks: Raw-data counterpart of every within-firm figure (Fig. 4 Panel A, Fig. 6, Fig. A11)
Measures recomputed on non-HQ establishments only (Fig. 6 Panel B, Fig. A9)
Restricting to firms with multiple establishments at some point in 1981-2016 (Figs. A1, A4, A5)
Maximum rather than average distance to the HQ (Fig. A5)
Alternative denominators for the manager ratio: adding business services, and adding business services and engineers (Fig. 11)
Alternative decomposition adding and subtracting the 2016 use share instead of the 1991 one (Appendix B.3)
unresolved_confounders: Establishments of Danish firms outside Denmark and arm's-length transactions inside the country are not observed
Possible changes in Statistics Denmark's definitions of firms and establishments over the sample period

estimator.value: Count of firms in the register (no regression)

claims.statement: The opening of establishments belonging to me firms is the main contributor to the 1991-2016 growth of the municipality-level manager ratio in 15 of Denmark's 98 municipalities.

definition.value: Calendar year; the reported estimate is the change in the yearly cross-sectional sample mean of the outcome between 1991 and 2016

outcome.label: Number of municipalities in which the opening of establishments belonging to ME firms is the main contributor to the growth of the manager-to-worker ratio

register_source.value: AKM (Labor Classification Module): the PSTILL variable and the 4-digit DISCO88 occupation code

definition.value: For each of the 98 municipalities, the change in the average establishment-level manager ratio is decomposed into changes within SE firms, within ME-firm establishments, and entry and exit; the municipality is assigned to the largest contributor

units.value: number of municipalities (out of 98) in which this is the main contributor

magnitude.interpretation: increases in the ratio of managers-to-workers inside ME firms and within firm fragmentation of such firms accounts for the reduction in the number of managers per worker in more than half of the country's municipalities

estimand.target_population: Danish municipalities

population.description: Firms (and their establishments) registered in Denmark in the private sector in manufacturing, transportation, business services and finance, insurance and real estate (FIRE), after the Appendix B.2 selection steps
subgroups_defined: 98 Danish municipalities
population.selection: Private-sector firms in manufacturing, transportation, business services and FIRE; establishments with no reported location or on three small islands dropped; establishments with 1 or 2 employees or appearing only one year dropped; firms with fewer than 4 employees for more than 66% of their existence dropped; firms with more than 99 establishments or large jumps in the number of establishments dropped (Appendix B.2, Table A5)

identification.source_of_variation: Year-to-year variation in cross-sectional sample means over 1981-2016; within-firm change and changes in the composition of firms are not separated

key_assumptions.assumption: The yearly cross-sectional averages are read as describing the economy as a whole; the paper states that their evolution also reflects changes in the composition of firms in the economy and not only change within firms
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper re-estimates the same quantity with firm fixed effects and compares the two

key_assumptions.assumption: The averages are computed on the selected sample (private-sector firms in manufacturing, transportation, business services and FIRE surviving the Appendix B.2 filters), not on the universe of Danish firms
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table A5 reports the observations left after each selection step

implies_edges.to: Number of municipalities in which the opening of establishments belonging to ME firms is the main contributor to the growth of the manager-to-worker ratio

key_assumptions.assumption: Establishments that Danish firms may have outside Denmark, and arm's-length transactions inside the country, are not observed, so the measured decentralization and specialization are a lower bound on the actual patterns

Statistics Denmark's definitions of firms and establishments did not change over 1981-2016 in a way that affects the results (the paper notes the firm fixed effects also help control for such changes)

threats_discussed: Changes in the composition of firms in the economy (entry and exit) contaminate raw-data averages: most entering firms are single-establishment and new firms are more compact
Establishments of Danish firms abroad and arm's-length transactions inside Denmark are unobserved, so the patterns are a lower bound
The average-distance measures include the distance of the HQ to itself (zeros), which lowers baseline distances and could inflate percentage changes
Possible changes over time in the way Statistics Denmark defines establishments
Including the HQ in the distance measures versus excluding it changes which firms contribute (excluding the HQ drops firms that go from one to multiple establishments)
robustness_checks: Raw-data counterpart of every within-firm figure (Fig. 4 Panel A, Fig. 6, Fig. A11)
Measures recomputed on non-HQ establishments only (Fig. 6 Panel B, Fig. A9)
Restricting to firms with multiple establishments at some point in 1981-2016 (Figs. A1, A4, A5)
Maximum rather than average distance to the HQ (Fig. A5)
Alternative denominators for the manager ratio: adding business services, and adding business services and engineers (Fig. 11)
Alternative decomposition adding and subtracting the 2016 use share instead of the 1991 one (Appendix B.3)
unresolved_confounders: Establishments of Danish firms outside Denmark and arm's-length transactions inside the country are not observed
Possible changes in Statistics Denmark's definitions of firms and establishments over the sample period

estimator.value: Municipality-level decomposition of the change in the average ratio (no regression reported)
